segments.t: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners
to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia,
we put to sea,
Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
The next day, we touched at Sidon.
Julius treated Paul kindly
and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
segments.note: 「refresh himself」は ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν（世話を受ける）の表現

segments.t: Putting to sea from there,
we sailed under the lee of Cyprus,
because the winds were contrary.
When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia,
we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
There the centurion found
a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy,
and he put us on board.
When we had sailed slowly many days,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus,
the wind not allowing us further,
we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
With difficulty sailing along it we came
to a certain place called Fair Havens,
near the city of Lasea.
When much time had passed
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and the voyage was now dangerous
because the Fast had now already gone by,
Paul admonished them
and said to them,
“Sirs,
I perceive that
the voyage will be with injury and much loss,
not only of the cargo and the ship,
but also of our lives.”
But the centurion
gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship
than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
Because the haven was not suitable to winter in,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: the majority advised going to sea from there,
if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there,
which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.
When the south wind blew softly,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: supposing that they had obtained their purpose,
they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
segments.note: 「close to shore」は ἆσσον の表現

segments.t: But before long,
a stormy wind beat down from shore,
which is called Euroclydon.
When the ship was caught
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and couldn’t face the wind,
we gave way to it and were driven along.
Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
After they had hoisted it up,
they used cables to help reinforce the ship.
Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars,
they lowered the sea anchor,
segments.note: σκεῦος（船具・錨具）を WEB は sea anchor とする

segments.t: and so were driven along.
As we labored exceedingly with the storm,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: the next day they began to throw things overboard.
On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and no small storm pressed on us,
all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
When they had been long without food,
Paul stood up in the middle of them and said,
“Sirs, you should have listened to me,
and not have set sail from Crete
and have gotten this injury and loss.
Now I exhort you to cheer up,
for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
For there stood by me this night an angel,
belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
saying,
‘Don’t be afraid, Paul.
You must stand before Caesar.
Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
Therefore, sirs, cheer up!
For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
But we must run aground on a certain island.”
But when the fourteenth night had come,
as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea,
about midnight
the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
They took soundings and found twenty fathoms.
After a little while,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground,
they let go four anchors from the stern,
and wished for daylight.
As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and had lowered the boat into the sea,
pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers,
“Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.
While the day was coming on,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: Paul begged them all to take some food,
saying,
“Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
Therefore I beg you to take some food,
for this is for your safety;
for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
When he had said this and had taken bread,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: he gave thanks to God in the presence of all;
then he broke it and began to eat.
Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: When they had eaten enough,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: they lightened the ship,
throwing out the wheat into the sea.
When it was day,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: they didn’t recognize the land,
but they noticed a certain bay with a beach,
and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea,
at the same time untying the rudder ropes.
Hoisting up the foresail to the wind,
they made for the beach.
But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground.
The bow struck and remained immovable,
but the stern began to break up by the violence
of the waves.
segments.note: WEB はビザンティン本文に従い τῶν κυμάτων（波の）を補う。ギリシャ語本文にこの語はない

segments.t: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: so that none of them would swim out and escape.
But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose,
and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
and the rest should follow,
some on planks
and some on other things from the ship.
So they all escaped safely to the land.
